icon_record.line: Central Texas housing. Army barracks in Texas and Louisiana. NASA habitat in Houston. Titan: its first system for outside builders.
facts: Announced 11 March 2026. ICON: multi-storey walls at roughly $20 a square foot, $5,000 deposit, training third quarter 2026, deliveries early 2027. ICON lists no price. Axios, All3DP: from $899,000. The Real Deal: leases first, sales first quarter 2027. Jason Ballard to Builder: the target is small and mid-sized builders.
Titan reservations include Ghost Factory, Cole Klein Builders and Moderne Development, per The Real Deal. Cole Klein builds Zuri Gardens, Houston, which HiveASMBLD prints.

100 homes with Lennar, designed by BIG. Printer: Vulcan. Announced 26 October 2021, printing by November 2022. Eight plans, 1,574 to 2,112 square feet, from the mid $400,000s. ICON calls it its first completed residential community (June 2026).

Community First! Village: 100 more, December 2024. Mueller: one-bedrooms from $195,000, about a dozen two- and three-bedrooms, printing from July 2025. Wimberley Springs: eight homes, upper $800,000s, July 2024.
Lennar's Houston division, its land arm Friendswood, and GreenEco, via Rausch Coleman, February 2025.

Mars Dune Alpha: 1,700 square foot NASA habitat at Johnson Space Center, 2021. Second crew mission inside: 19 October 2025 to 31 October 2026. No ICON housing in Houston, per its own site. HiveASMBLD has repeat production work here, PERI a house inside city limits.

Fort Bliss, El Paso: ten barracks, 78,000 square feet, up to 560 soldiers, $62.8 million. ICON announced delivery 28 July 2026. The Army: two open that day, the rest in September. ICON and the Army: the military's largest robotic construction deployment. Fort Polk, Louisiana: $67.9 million, March 2026, vertical construction from September 2026.
Government division launched 14 April 2026. President: Will Hurd. Over $360 million in government contracts, per ICON.

Structures completed: over 245 per ICON in March 2026, 263 on its site now. TechCrunch: 114 layoffs filed January 2025, over a quarter of staff. $56 million Series C, February 2025, led by Norwest and Tiger Global.

Company filings, company pages, trade press. Each contact names its page: 109 LinkedIn headlines naming the firm, 173 firm sites or dated reports, 14 names with no page to link. No aggregator. Nothing inferred.

code.line: Houston: no zoning, the 2021 IRC, and no 3D-printing appendix.

items.a: No. Houston has no zoning. Chapter 42: subdivision, setbacks, parking. Masterplan deed restrictions can refuse an exterior material.
items.source: City of Houston Planning, Development Regulations

items.a: 2021 IRC, in force 1 January 2024. Appendix AW not adopted. Printed walls enter under R104.11, alternative materials and methods, on an ICC-ES report to AC509.
Yes. ESR-4652, reissued June 2026: bearing, non-bearing and shear walls to 12 feet. Seismic Design Categories A and B. Special inspection.
The county seat's IRC (LGC 233.153). Third-party inspection at foundation, framing and completion (233.154). Houston is Harris County's seat.

items.q: Can a city or county refuse it?
items.a: Not if a national model code approves it within three cycles. Government Code Chapter 3000, effective 1 September 2019. Exceptions: historic districts, state- or federally-funded housing.
items.source: Texas Government Code 3000 and TML Q&A

method.title: Printer-fit bands
method.text: An assumption, not a published figure. Yes: 25 to 400 homes a year, one or two printers, at up to about 200 houses a year per Titan. Published rates are slower. Wolf Ranch: one Vulcan and crew, about three weeks a home by August 2024, about seventeen a year (Engadget, 8 August 2024).
